EN.bani: Finding one person's or brand's accounts across many sites takes a long time. This project automates it, so one command checks all the sites.
EN.job: Security researchers, OSINT analysts (people who research using public information), journalists, brand teams.
EN.kahan: Security research, investigations, brand protection, digital safety training.
EN.kya: Sherlock takes a username and checks 400+ social networks to see where an account with that name exists. The accounts it finds are saved in a text file.
EN.need: If you want to protect your brand name or do research, you need to see where a username is used. For example, you start a new business and check whether the name is free on Instagram, X and GitHub.
EN.rn: Medium risk because it automatically checks many sites (question 5), and some sites' rules may not allow that. It can affect someone's privacy, so use it only on your own names or with permission. It can also include 18+ sites (this is controlled by an option).
EN.type: Tool that finds social media accounts from a username
win: You need Python. In the terminal: `pipx install sherlock-project`
Or with Docker: `docker run -it --rm sherlock/sherlock`
To run it: `sherlock user123` (replace user123 with the username)
